# mITyGuitar Desktop 0.0.1

## What's New
- Desktop application release for Windows
- Full featured guitar learning and practice application
- Chord mapping and song chart support
- Controller integration for interactive practice

### Windows Installers
- **MSI Package**: `mITyGuitar_0.0.1_x64_en-US.msi` - Windows Installer Package (recommended for most users)

- Windows 10/11 (64-bit)

## mITyStudio v1.1.20

Automated Windows build of `master` @ 6c8646c.

**Installing over a previous version updates in place** — your
workspace (projects, soundfonts, samples, voices) lives outside the
install directory and is preserved.

![Studio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/janvanwassenhove/mITyStudio/6c8646ce30be78634252768fec77c5954470c489/docs/screenshots/studio.png)
![First-start guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/janvanwassenhove/mITyStudio/6c8646ce30be78634252768fec77c5954470c489/docs/screenshots/onboarding.png)
![Voices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/janvanwassenhove/mITyStudio/6c8646ce30be78634252768fec77c5954470c489/docs/screenshots/voices.png)

### Changes
Nav: icons instead of labels, so Assets/Voices/Settings stay reachable

Reported: could no longer navigate to Assets, Voices or Settings.

Cause: .topnav is a single flex row with no wrap and no overflow handling.
Brand + four translated labels + three panel toggles + theme + about +
language select + a status label ("backend verbonden") exceed the width of a
narrower window — and on desktop the title-bar overlay eats the right side
too — so the last items were pushed out of reach with no way to scroll to
them. Dutch and German labels are the longest, which is why it showed up
here first.

The four destinations are now icons (audio lines / library / mic / sliders)
with their translated names as tooltip + aria-label, which is both what was
asked for and ~200px narrower. Made the bar structurally overflow-proof
rather than just smaller: brand, buttons, toggles and the language select
are flex:none, and the status label is the only element allowed to collapse
(its text hides under 900px, leaving the coloured dot). The active route now
reads as an accent-tinted pill instead of bold text.

scrum.changelog: # SCRUM v2.0.0 ## 🧠 New Language Feature: `#INTENT` SCRUM introduces **`#INTENT`**, enabling developers to express logic in natural language that is transformed into executable SCRUM code **at compile time**. ### Key characteristics - Natural language → SCRUM code - Executed at **compile time** - Powered by LLMs with **automatic provider fallback** - Generated code is validated and re-parsed - **No runtime AI dependency** ### Example ```scrum EPIC "StatisticsApp" USER STORY "ComputeStats" #INTENT I want to create a list of 5 numbers, calculate their sum and average, and display the results in a readable format. #END INTENT END OF USER STORY END OF EPIC StatisticsApp IS NEW StatisticsApp StatisticsApp::ComputeStats USING [] ``` During compilation, the #INTENT block is processed by the configured LLM provider. SCRUM generates valid SCRUM code, validates it, and executes it like any handwritten implementation. Same determinism. Less boilerplate. Zero AI magic at runtime. --- ## ☕ Platform Upgrade - **Upgraded to **Java 25** (LTS)** SCRUM now runs on the latest long-term support JVM, bringing improved performance, stability, and long-term maintainability. --- ## 📦 Fully Standalone SDK SCRUM is now distributed as a **complete, installable SDK**, allowing it to be used independently without manual JAR execution. ### What’s included - Cross-platform installers (Windows, Linux, macOS) - Global `scrum` CLI available on the PATH - No manual Java command invocation required - Bundled: - Examples - Documentation - CLI tooling SCRUM can now be installed, executed, and integrated like a first-class programming language. --- ## 🧰 Developer Experience Improvements - Enhanced CLI support: -

aura.changelog:
# AURA v2.0.112

_Your own robot colleague — he knows your household, joins the conversation, and keeps quiet when that serves you better._

This release brings **one improvement**, from something that went wrong or was missing in real use.

## What's new and better

- I handed him a sentence to hide behind

## What it looks like

![01-operator-console.png](https://github.com/janvanwassenhove/aura/releases/download/v2.0.112/01-operator-console.png)

_Captured on a fresh demo install: the fictional demo profile only, never real personal data._

## Getting started

| Your system | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows | `AURA-*-windows-setup.exe` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon, M1–M4) | `AURA-*-mac-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS (Intel) | `AURA-*-mac-x64.dmg` |
| Linux | `AURA-*-linux-x86_64.AppImage` or `.deb` |

**First time?** Download, install, and start it. On first launch AURA sets itself up (a few minutes) and a short wizard walks you through your robot, your voice and your language.

**Already on an older version?** Install straight over it — your people, your memories and your settings stay exactly as they are.

<details><summary>macOS and Linux: one extra click the first time</summary>

The macOS builds are not notarised: open them the first time via right-click → Open. On macOS and Linux the first launch installs the Python runtime (uv) by itself.
</details>

## Why AURA

AURA turns a Reachy Mini into a housemate rather than a device: he recognises who is in front of him, remembers what you tell him, co-presents with you and can watch your screen — **and all of it stays on your own machine**. No subscription, no cloud profile: your keys and your memories are encrypted on this computer.

---

The full technical history of every change is in [docs/implementation-backlog.md](https://github.com/janvanwassenhove/aura/blob/master/docs/implementation-backlog.md).

BullyOff.changelog:
**BULLY OFF** — a deterministic field-hockey manager. Coach a fictional Belgian club through a season that is really played, minute by minute, in your browser: https://janvanwassenhove.github.io/BullyOff/

Offline-first PWA · no accounts, no telemetry, no real clubs or people · NL / EN / FR.

## Versions

- Engine **0.8.0** (sandbox golden `7511507816fd5c49`) — deterministic, dependency-free, SI units end to end.
- Save format **v4** (linear migrations from v1; team sheet, PC battery and captain live in the save).

## Calibration (96 matches per profile, level 12 ± 2, watered turf)

- **Men: 14/15 bands · Women: 12/15 — every directly-measured metric passes in both.**
- Men: 5.20 goals/match, 10.1 penalty corners, 34 % of goals from PC+PS, strokes 0.25 at 67 % conversion, cards in band.
- Women: 3.66 goals/match, 8.5 corners, 31 % PC share, stroke conversion 76 %.
- Known deviations (all at the edge of *estimated* bands, full log in `docs/rules/calibration.md`): women's circle entries and restart volume a whisker under, shots a whisker over; the men's scoreline-shape test flips with the seed set (a ±2-level league is genuinely top-heavy).

## What the coach gets

Team sheet with bench and rest days, signed before kick-off · tactics board on a to-scale FIH pitch with the real press and back lines · penalty-corner battery, variants picked in-match from the players actually on the pitch · opponent scouting that only reports what was actually played · in-match coaching with rolling subs · a rulebook with pitch and figure animations checked against the FIH rules, plus verified explainer videos · an academy that teaches the game the engine actually plays · works on phone, tablet and laptop, as webapp and installed PWA.

## Owed human reviews (do not block the build — `KICKOFF.md`)

The on-phone manual checklist in `docs/release.md` (install, offline relaunch, 60 fps coached match, save export/import, update banner) awaits Jan's device pass.
